the “it can’t be done not possible” argument is the most lazy thing I’ve ever heard. I can sit here and report for advertisement over and over all day, sure. Or blizzard could just pay gms to do for everyone instead of me doing it.

And that would be just to deal with them atm as a short term problem. I would want a long term solution that combines multiple angles of dealing with them. There are different methods I imagine that would work in combination. People say you can’t do word filter because they will just change the words they use but all blizzard has to do is look at lfg and see what they’re adapting too. A smaller character limit for description might also help to reduce them. With a shorter number of words or letters they have to be more effecient with how they advertise thus greatly reducing the room they have to make their sells pitch and making it easier to filter out their work arounds. I don’t even know a valid argument for group descriptions to be more than 20 characters max.

“Lust” “Healer,” “Tank” “resil” like all of these terms the community finds essential are less than 20 characters. A rmt boost seller has to make it clear what their listing is, what its for, and how to get into contact with them. Disable being able to whisper group leaders (already the case for cross faction group leaders anyway where I can’t whisper a horde party leader of a key listing,) and then filter out their websites like “chaos boost” “wowvendor” etc.

And just have some gms actually dedicated to clearing it out as well. It would be better for the gms to be proactive about clearing out the listings instead of waiting for reports from us reactively. A human gm can just look at booster listings and determine it is what it is and take action on the account more quickly than waiting for an account or accounts to rack up violations or whatever method they are using at the moment.

Email domain bans for those using temp emails or similar methods to create accounts, standard hardware/ip bans or even IP Range ban, etc.

Can blizzard bring a law suit against the people who are perpetrating these sorts of exploitative, rule breaking behaviors?

Perhaps there are more unique solutions alone or in combination that would reduce or stop booster ad listings and I want to know from blizzard that they are working toward this end. So far they are silent about it and lfg is polluted by it.

At the very least they need to re-assign a few gm’s from general support to eliminating the ads and actioning the offending accounts in the short term until a long term solution is found.

I already pointed out in this thread that the people advertising in LFG are RMT services. Real Money Transfer. They do not accept gold for their services. Blizzard makes no money from them, because no token or cash is exchanged with blizzard.

Both advertising in lfg and RMT are against the rules. ChaosBoost and all those other ones are literally advertising their websites. If you go investigate like I did trying to find an email address to write an angry email to, you’ll see on their home pages that they are asking for cash. Often in the hundreds of dollars.

Which, besides possibly being an outright scam to fool gullible people, feels like it should be illegal but is at least actually against blizzard’s ToS. Blizzard doesn’t make money from these third parties taking a buyers money directly. They have no place in the exchange of cash and no gold is involved.

I think it’s a bit strange that the boost advertisers are going so hard at it. They are either desperate for money or they’re making so much money they can afford to keep making accounts for this purpose.

It is quite dumb, but there are player-side solutions that don’t take very long, and honestly will just be better for you in the long run as is. I run the Premade Groups Filter addon, and I basically never see these in these channels. It has the bonus of just being a great addon for filtering out incompatible groups, which saves a lot of wasted time looking for keys.

For keys, I filter using a minimum score (500ish on alts, or 2400 on my main), and it works to make them nonexistent as most of them are posting on bots with no score at all, usually low level or trial characters with no access to the content.

For raids, just filter using the members section to filter for a minimum of 2 players. I have yet to see a post that has more than one bot, and I see zero ads there either.
